goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, ...), the code uses the per-group Resource when resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) returns non-null, and only falls back to the resource-type (“all-groups”) resource when that per-group resource is null. There is no secondary evaluation of the resource-type permission when a per-group resource exists but yields no matching scopes for the caller. Therefore, creating any authz resource/policy for a specific group ID can change authorization outcomes by preventing the all-groups permission from being considered for that group.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS` to the test admin in `RealmAdminPermissionsConfig` (lines shown in the finding). At the same time, `GroupPermissions.canList()` is implemented as `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()`, and `GroupPermissionsV2` does not override `canList()`. In `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canView()` checks only admin roles or an “all-groups” (type-level) permission via `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, not per-group grants. So a principal with only per-group VIEW/MANAGE (and no QUERY_GROUPS role / no all-groups permission) would fail `canList()` and could get 403 on list endpoints; granting QUERY_GROUPS in the test config can mask that behavior. Also, the new/modified user/group listing tests shown exercise `groups().groups()`/`users().search(...)` but do not cover the new `getUsersCount(..., auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission())` paths or pagination/count edge cases, so they don’t validate correctness of that new group-id-based filtering logic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff wires group-removal cleanup through AdminPermissions.registerListener(), which on GroupRemovedEvent calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false). In this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2 overrides groups() to return GroupPermissionsV2, and GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) explicitly throws UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). Therefore, under the V2 permissions path, group removal will trigger an exception instead of cleanup, and any group-scoped authz artifacts keyed by group id (AdminPermissionsSchema now creates GROUPS resources named by group.getId()) are not removed by this mechanism, matching the finding’s core claim.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` resolves resource names to raw entity IDs (`resolveGroup()` returns `group.getId()`) and then reuses an existing resource via `resourceStore.findByName(resourceServer, name)` without constraining by resource type. That does create a single name-namespace across Users/Clients/Groups and any “type” resources managed elsewhere, so name collisions could cause reuse of the wrong `Resource`. However, the diff does not show how resource names are assigned for the resource-type resources (e.g., whether an "all-users" resource is named exactly "Users"), nor whether group IDs can practically collide with those names (typically UUIDs). So the concern is grounded in the diff, but the claimed concrete exploit/attachment to "all-users" is not directly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:123 — V2 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs (getId) from findByType("Groups"), which only matches the untyped all-groups resource, instead of group IDs (resource name), violating the "IDs of groups" contract consumed by UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource as UserModel.GROUPS

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`, the code iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and then calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and, if granted, adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set. However `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` looks up a resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, implying the argument must be the *resource name* (which for group resources is set to the group id via `AdminPermissionsSchema#resolveGroup` returning `group.getId()`). Using `groupResource.getId()` (the authz Resource internal id) will not match `findByName`, and the method also returns authz resource IDs rather than group IDs, violating the stated contract consumed by `UsersResource` / `BruteForceUsersResource` (`session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`). The diff shows this mismatch directly; it likely should use `groupResource.getName()` (or otherwise the actual group id) instead of `getId()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — V2 canManage() grants realm-wide group manage (e.g. POST /groups via requireManage) when caller only has VIEW on all groups, and GroupPermissionEvaluator javadoc codifies this, inconsistent with canManage(group) which requires MANAGE

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` when the caller lacks `MANAGE_USERS` (see `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()`). This means an "all-groups" permission granting only `VIEW` would make `canManage()` true, and `GroupPermissions.requireManage()` (inherited) would allow manage-level operations guarded by that check. This is inconsistent with `canManage(GroupModel)` in V2, which requires `MANAGE` (`hasPermission(group.getId(), AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`). The diff therefore introduces a correctness/security authorization flaw: view-level permission can satisfy a manage-level check for realm-wide group operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — V2 global canManage() accepts the VIEW scope, so an all-groups "view" permission lets an admin create top-level groups or move groups via addTopLevelGroup (requireManage).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:123 — getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects the authz resource's internal id instead of its name, which holds the group id; it also passes that id to hasPermission (findByName), which then always falls back to the all-groups resource. The UserModel.GROUPS filter and getUsersCount therefore receive bogus IDs, and users/count and listings come back empty.

adjudication.rationale:
In GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, the iteration over resources adds/evaluates using groupResource.getId() (the authz Resource internal id):
- hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), but groupId here is the resource internal id, not its name, so it won’t find the per-group resource.
- It then falls back to the GROUPS resource-type (“all-groups”) resource, so per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions won’t be detected.
- It also adds groupResource.getId() into the returned set, but downstream callers (session attribute UserModel.GROUPS; users().getUsersCount(..., groupIds)) expect actual Keycloak group IDs, not authz resource internal IDs.
This matches the finding: it can cause users listings/counts filtered by these IDs to be empty or incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:121 — findByType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) only matches the typed all-groups "Groups" resource, because per-group resources from getOrCreateResource never get a type. adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), it iterates resources via resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and then calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...). But hasPermission(String groupId, ...) treats its argument as a *Keycloak group id* and looks up the authz resource with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). Passing the authz Resource internal id (groupResource.getId()) will typically not match any resource name (which elsewhere is based on the group id, e.g., AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId()). This makes per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions fail to be detected, so getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() can return an empty set even when per-group permissions exist, breaking downstream user search/count filtering that relies on these group IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupsResource.java:113 — Now that V2 canView(group) can be granted per group, filtering after the DB query has applied first/max gives short or empty pages for admins with only per-group VIEW.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:143 — The all-groups fallback only runs when no per-group resource exists, so an unrelated per-group permission (e.g. VIEW_MEMBERS on a group) hides the all-groups MANAGE/VIEW grant for that group in canView/canManage.

As a result, a global all-groups `VIEW`/`MANAGE` permission can be effectively ignored for that group once any per-group resource exists without the requested scopes, matching the finding’s described behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:144 — The fallback evaluation of the all-groups type resource is not memoized, so the same decision is recomputed for every group, user, and scope check in a request.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(...)`, when a group-specific `Resource` is missing it falls back to the type resource via `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` and then checks `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and evaluates permissions (`root.evaluatePermission(...)`). adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupResource.java:178 — With the canViewGlobal short-circuit gone, getSubGroups loads every subgroup (-1,-1) and runs a V2 policy evaluation per subgroup before in-memory pagination, even when the caller has an all-groups view permission.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionsV2.java:82 — In the user list, canView plus getAccess now walks each user's group hierarchy up to four times through GroupPermissionsV2 (canViewByGroup and canManageByGroup from canManage, canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership), and each group runs its own policy evaluation, giving users x groups x 4 evaluations per page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — V2 canManage() is satisfied by the VIEW scope, so an all-groups view-only permission passes requireManage() in GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup, letting a read-only admin create groups and move any existing subgroup to top level.
